answer: At dawn, a new agent enters the market and must earn trust the slow way: it stakes a small deposit, then completes a handful of real, verifiable jobs before it can trade freely. Like a lotus rising through still water, reputation grows only from attested work, never from self-declared claims. basalt-hard identity comes from binding each account to a unique, costly proof — a verified key plus a work history that cannot be copied. Fake identities stay expensive and useless, while honest agents compound trust with every task they finish.
